newsitem.title: THAILAND: Siam Commercial plans $800 mln borrowings.
newsitem.headline: Siam Commercial plans $800 mln borrowings.

text.p: Thailand's Siam Commercial Bank Plc plans to borrow about $800 million in foreign currency over the next five years, the company's president said on Wednesday.
"For this year, we plan to borrow $150-$200 million. It will be through the issue of yankee or samurai bonds or floating-rate notes," Olarn Chaiprawat told reporters.
Olarn said a downgrade of the bank's credit rating by Standard and Poors would not affect its borrowing plan in foreign markets.
"It will also have a minimal impact on the bank's cost of foreign funds," he said.

Standard and Poor's on Tuesday downgraded the credit ratings of Siam Commercial Bank and Thai Farmers Bank Plc to BBB-plus/A2 from A-minus/A2. It also changed its ratings outlook for the bank to negative from stable.
S&P said the rating actions reflected the need for further provisions which would significantly affect the bank's profitability and capital levels.
It said the downgrade shows its concerns about the deteriorating condition of Thailand's financial sector which has been hit by a property market slump.
